subject: Saving factor scores in each imputed dataset

messages.author: e8c7f8fdbee6558e
messages.subject: Saving factor scores in each imputed dataset
parts:
Dear all,

I am running a CFA using a list of multiple imputed datasets (using runMI ( ...fun="cfa")) and I would like to save the factor scores (e.g. using lavPredict()) in each imputed dataset. I then want to use those factor scores in other analyses (e.g. correlations), by pooling the results of these other analyses using runMI().

How can I save the factor scores in each imputed dataset, using the output of a fitted model that was produced by runMI()? 

Many thanks! 

Andrea Cortes

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Saving factor scores in each imputed dataset
parts:
Maybe this will help:

library(lavaan)
library(Amelia)

HSMiss <- HolzingerSwineford1939[ , c(paste("x", 1:9, sep = ""),
                                      "ageyr","agemo","school")]
set.seed(12345)
HSMiss$x5 <- ifelse(HSMiss$x5 <= quantile(HSMiss$x5, .3), NA, HSMiss$x5)
age <- HSMiss$ageyr + HSMiss$agemo/12
HSMiss$x9 <- ifelse(age <= quantile(age, .3), NA, HSMiss$x9)

## specify CFA model from lavaan's ?cfa help page
HS.model <- '
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'

## impute data within runMI...
out <- cfa.mi(HS.model, data = HSMiss, m = 2, seed = 12345,
               miArgs = list(noms = "school"))


res <- list(
  s1 = lavPredict(cfa(HS.model, data = out@DataList$imp1)),
  s2 = lavPredict(cfa(HS.model, data = out@DataList$imp2))
)

res

Notes:
I suspect that runMi stores the imputed data here: @DataList$impX. But I don't know for sure and I didn't check it. So be careful :-)
Of course, if there are many imputations, it makes more sense to develop a loop to process everything. So the code above is only a very simplified example. And again: The solution could be wrong ...

messages.subject: Re: Saving factor scores in each imputed dataset
parts:
If you install the latest development version of semTools, I added an example to the ?plausibleValues help page for merging to imputations.  Hopefully that is what you intend to use, since you should take into account the uncertainty of estimated factors scores (they are missing data, too).
